summary: Example: SingleCommit and ClaimedEventuallyDone hold for 2 workers and 1 job with at most 3 claims (25 distinct states); the same model without the fencing check reaches a double commit in 6 steps.

modeled: runJob: claim, work, commit with a fencing token
lease expiry as an environment action
abstracted: the work itself is one step
one job row; more rows are symmetric
out_of_scope: worker crashes between claim and commit
clock skew between workers and the database
assumptions: A1: db.claim and db.commit are each one atomic statement
A2: the lease can expire at any moment while a worker is working

properties.name: SingleCommit
properties.meaning: At most one worker commits the job.

properties.name: ClaimedEventuallyDone
properties.meaning: Once someone holds a claim, the job gets done.
properties.bounds: Workers={w1,w2}, MaxClaims=3, UseFencing=TRUE, weak fairness on Commit and Abort

properties.name: SingleCommit (bug mode)
properties.meaning: The same invariant with UseFencing=FALSE: it must fail, which shows the check can fail.

findings.title: A worker whose lease expired can still commit the job
findings.story: Worker w2 claims the job and stalls past its lease. The lease expires, worker w1 claims the job and commits it. When w2 wakes up, its commit is not checked against the row's token, so it commits as well and the job is committed twice. This trace is from the model without the fencing check; the shipped code has the check, so the example shows the shape of a finding, not a bug in the code.

sanity_checks: MC_sanity.cfg violates NoReclaim, so a reclaim after expiry is reachable
